instruction: Use the already opened Bonsai/Blender IFC authoring environment and its CLI/API tools to update /home/user/Desktop/init.ifc and save the finished model as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc. For this workflow, Bonsai is installed as a Blender extension, so start `/opt/blender/blender` and use the Bonsai tools from that environment. Do not create, rewrite, copy, patch, or post-process the IFC outside that software environment. The model is a small exposed supply-air duct run serving two terminals in a compact plantroom mock-up. The mechanical contractor needs the air-side network to behave as one verified supply system rather than disconnected products. Preserve the existing duct segment, fitting, and terminal geometry, but organise them under a single supply-air system, add and name the missing connection ports, and create exactly six unique cross-product port connections so all seven products form one connected commissioning network. Do not create reverse duplicate relations, self-connections, or product-internal connections. Stamp the system and assigned products with revision code BONSAI-CLI-07. Deterministic evaluation contract: the identifiers, counts, relationships, properties, and numeric ranges in the following JSON are explicit task requirements: {"automation":{"AutomationStatus":"CLI_UPDATED","TaskCode":"BONSAI-CLI-07"},"counts":{"IfcAirTerminal":2,"IfcDistributionPort":12,"IfcDistributionSystem":1,"IfcDuctFitting":2,"IfcDuctSegment":3,"IfcRelConnectsPorts":6},"members":["Main Segment","Branch Spine","Riser Segment","Transition","Bend","Terminal East","Terminal North"],"system_name":"Supply Air Verified"}.
